question: For matched populations, how do t, percentile and BCa mean intervals change coverage, width and miss direction on the same samples?

randomness.replicate_ids: 0..1999 inclusive, each with its own original and resampling streams
randomness.pairing: all 3 methods share the same original sample; percentile and BCa share exactly the same bootstrap mean vector
randomness.independence: distinct outer replicates have independently keyed original and resampling streams; no common index array is broadcast across replicates; seed IDs alone are not proof of independence

methods.t: existing unknown-variance ddof=1, df=n-1 two-sided t interval

bca.no_fallback: no clipping or substitution with t/percentile when BCa is undefined

methods.finite_bootstrap: evaluate the finite B_boot=999 procedure, not B_boot->infinity or a separate inner-MC convergence study

invalid_policy.reasons: nonfinite sample, n<2, constant sample, nonfinite z0/a, bad adjusted quantile order and other undefined numerical outputs remain reason-labelled invalid
invalid_policy.main_aggregates: any invalid method interval makes its unconditional rates and width summaries NA; total R and valid/invalid counts remain explicit
invalid_policy.pair_aggregates: any invalid paired interval makes main paired differences NA; joint-valid reference values are explicitly prefixed conditional_ and never used for decisions
invalid_policy.tail_warning: B_boot*min(q,1-q)<10 at either endpoint; recorded separately, does not invalidate or change the method

summaries.miss_above: lower > true mean (interval wholly above truth)
summaries.miss_below: upper < true mean (interval wholly below truth)
summaries.decision_rates: 99% Wilson intervals, columns separate from descriptive 95% intervals
summaries.width: mean, median, sample SD ddof=1, MCSE=SD/sqrt(R), 99% mean +/- z(.995)*MCSE
summaries.paired: per-outer-replicate coverage indicator and width differences, sample SD ddof=1 / sqrt(R); preserve sums and sums of squares
summaries.pooling: sum sufficient statistics over the 3 seed cells (6000 independent outer replicates), never treat 3 seed means as sample size 3; pooled median uses saved interval widths only

decision.scope: hypotheses refer only to centered_exponential; normal is reference, n=100 descriptive
decision.confidence: each of 5 preregistered quantities uses a 99% interval, a Bonferroni-type approximate familywise 95% decision; paired normal approximation is not an exact simultaneous guarantee
decision.support: all relevant pooled 99% intervals satisfy the strict desired inequalities and every seed point estimate is strictly on the same desired side of its threshold
decision.not_supported: at least one relevant interval lies completely on the opposite side (strictly beyond threshold); record this contrary evidence before discussing mixed seeds
decision.inconclusive: interval touches/straddles threshold, mixed seed directions, any invalid or incomplete cell; contrary intervals are separately recorded
decision.normal_t_gate: all 9 normal t coverage counts in inclusive binom.ppf(epsilon/(2*9),R,.95)..binom.ppf(1-epsilon/(2*9),R,.95), epsilon=.001; unresolved reference checks prevent a final scientific conclusion
decision.prohibitions: no threshold changes, seed selection, method additions, extra R/B/n or redraws in response to outcomes

execution.main: once only; bug correction at most one separately authorized attempt retaining reason, old source and old outputs, cumulative main wall <=600 seconds
execution.smoke: one separately authorized R=2,B_boot=99 check over 18 cells (36 outer samples) in smoke namespace; never used to choose hypotheses/design
execution.over_budget: save completed and incomplete cells, stop; no automatic resizing, expansion or rerun
execution.retained: endpoints, valid/reason/tail flags only; never raw samples or full bootstrap arrays
